item.title: Mamdani Unveils Rikers Island Shutdown Plan
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Mayor Mamdani wants extra runway for NYC’s overhaul of incarceration, including one of America’s most infamous lockups.
item.content:encoded:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan Friday to close New York City’s Rikers Island jail complex by 2032 because construction delays and a jail population of about 6,600 put the city’s 2027 deadline out of reach. 

Mayor Mamdani’s proposal would replace Rikers with four smaller jails across the city, starting with a downtown Brooklyn facility scheduled to open in 2029. That would put the first replacement jail roughly two years behind the date the city had set for shutting down the entire island complex. 

Rikers Island has been part of Hip-Hop’s account of New York for decades. Kool G Rap and DJ Polo turned the jail’s reputation for violence into a warning on “Riker’s Island,” while Lil Wayne documented his eight months there in 2010 in Gone ’Til November: A Journal of Rikers Island.

Jay-Z brought the story of a Bronx teenager to a national audience as an executive producer of the 2017 documentary series Time: The Kalief Browder Story. Browder spent three years at Rikers awaiting trial before prosecutors dropped the charges. His case puts a human face on one of the biggest questions in Mamdani’s shutdown plan: how long New York keeps people in jail while they wait for their day in court.

The legal deadline is still Aug. 31, 2027. The City Council would have to amend the 2019 law that set it. Council Speaker Julie Menin said delays under previous administrations had made more time necessary to carry out the closure.

“It is time to finally close Rikers Island,” Mamdani said in a statement. “For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane.” 

“For decades, New Yorkers have demanded a correctional system that is safe and humane. This plan puts us on a path to deliver just that: closing Rikers, reducing pretrial detention, tackling the case delays that deprives people of their right to a speedy trial and investing $146 million in evidence-based supports that help break the cycles of incarceration,” he continued. “We have a legal and moral obligation to close Rikers. Working alongside the City Council, Courts and nonprofit partners, we will meet it — for the people in our custody, the staff who serve them, victims of crime, and every New Yorker.”

The construction schedule is only part of the plan. The administration aims to bring the jail population down to 5,500 by the time the Brooklyn facility opens and to 4,100 by 2032. City officials are counting on faster court proceedings and expanded alternatives to detention to help reach those targets. The plan also calls for restoring online bail payments in 2027 after the city’s portal went offline in 2023.

The administration plans to spend $146 million next fiscal year on services that include mental health care, substance use treatment, education, job training and support for crime victims. It also plans to add 236 hospital beds in Brooklyn and the Bronx for people in custody with serious mental health conditions or complex medical needs.

Rikers has faced years of scrutiny over violence, deteriorating facilities and deaths in custody. A federal judge placed the complex under the authority of an outside official last year after the city failed to improve conditions. Mamdani said his administration developed the closure plan in consultation with that official and would continue working with him as it carries out the proposal.

For families, the geography of the plan matters as much as the date.

The city says a trip to Rikers can take hours and consume an entire day. The replacement jails would sit closer to courthouses, public transit and the neighborhoods where people in custody live.

If the city meets its new timetable, the change could be felt in something as ordinary as how long it takes to see someone you love.

item.title: Post Malone Opens The “Stoney” Vault With Eight Songs And A One-Night Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Post Malone marks 10 years of Stoney with a Hollywood Palladium show and eight vault tracks, including one with Leon Thomas.
item.content:encoded:
Post Malone is bringing his first album back with eight recordings that didn’t make the original release.

The expanded Stoney is due December 11, two days after a one-night show at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles. One of the eight songs, “Free” with Leon Thomas, will be available only on streaming.

The December 9 concert falls exactly ten years after Stoney came out. In an Apple Music interview, Post and his father looked back at how quickly things changed when “White Iverson” caught on.

Post had broken through with “White Iverson” before he released an album.

As he finished Stoney, he told iHeart he wanted the record to capture what happened when he worked with people he liked as artists and friends.

He was also putting more instruments into the sessions. “I play guitar on the album, that’s pretty tight,” he said.

Post had pushed back the album’s planned August release before it arrived in December.

The title came from a nickname he remembered from before the record deal: “Whenever I used to smoke weed, everybody would call me ‘Stoney Maloney.'”

The finished record put his guitar-led “Go Flex” alongside “Congratulations” with Quavo and “Deja Vu” with Justin Bieber. “Congratulations,” “White Iverson” and “I Fall Apart” all went Diamond.

By September 2022, Stoney had spent 300 weeks on the Billboard 200.

The original deluxe tracks are appearing on vinyl for the first time. The anniversary release will also come on two CDs and a double cassette, and the CD set includes a poster.

Post Malone’s store is limiting the slime-green three-LP set to 7,000 copies worldwide.

item.title: Robert Glasper Says New Track For “14th” With Brittany Howard Gave Him Freedom To Create
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Robert Glasper and Brittany Howard join forces for Ava DuVernay's '14th,' a decade after his Emmy-winning work on '13th.'
item.content:encoded:
Robert Glasper is back in Ava DuVernay’s world a decade after making an Emmy-winning song for 13th.

This time, the pianist and producer has Alabama Shakes singer Brittany Howard alongside him on “Makings of Tomorrow,” a new song for the director’s Netflix documentary 14th.

The single came out via Netflix Music, ahead of the film’s theatrical release.

“Brittany has one of those voices that makes you stop what you’re doing and listen. She brings so much soul and honesty to the music, and that gives me a lot of freedom as a collaborator. Creating this song together for Ava’s film ’14th’ was an opportunity to put that connection into something with real purpose,” Glasper told AllHipHop.com.

The DuVernay connection goes back to “Letter to the Free.” Glasper and Karriem Riggins wrote the music alongside Common, who also wrote the lyrics. The three won the 2017 Emmy for Outstanding Original Music and Lyrics, then kept working together as August Greene.

Glasper has his own history with Howard, too. He played keyboards on four tracks from her 2019 solo debut Jaime and joined her for live dates, according to Island Records.

The song also plays in Netflix’s trailer for the documentary.

Two of the musicians from those Jaime sessions, Glasper and Alabama Shakes bassist Zac Cockrell, play on the new single.

Cage the Elephant guitarist Nick Bockrath and Glasper’s drummer, Justin Tyson, also play on the track.

Howard described the job of writing for the documentary.

“Creating this song came with great responsibility since it needed to capture the urgency and importance of the film. We hope ‘Makings of Tomorrow’ will inspire people to stand up and fight for those whose rights are being taken from them unjustly. We are all in need of a better tomorrow.”

The film follows DuVernay’s look at the 13th Amendment and the legacy of slavery, examining the 14th Amendment, which includes protections for birthright citizenship and equal protection under the law. It screened as the closing-night film at the New York Film Festival in October.

14th opens in select theaters on November 27 and streams on Netflix starting December 4.

item.title: Michael Jackson Estate Deal Leads Cascio Family To Sue Bryan Freedman
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: The Cascio siblings and James Porte allege Bryan Freedman failed to disclose his ties to Michael Jackson's estate.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Jackson’s former family friends are suing the attorney who helped broker their deal with his estate.

Five Cascio siblings and James Porte allege Bryan Freedman let them sign away legal rights in 2019 and 2020 without telling them he was working for the estate.

The civil suit was filed November 18 in Los Angeles County Superior Court, Rolling Stone reported.

Frank, Edward, Dominic, Aldo and Marie-Nicole are plaintiffs alongside James, Marie-Nicole’s husband. The complaint names Freedman alone and accuses him of malpractice, breach of fiduciary duty, fraud and negligent misrepresentation.

A separate court filing shows Freedman represented Edward and James in a dispute over a posthumous Jackson album.

The new suit alleges that after HBO aired Leaving Neverland in 2019, the estate sent him to arrange a deal with the family. The plaintiffs say Freedman told them they didn’t need their own lawyer.

The family says the deal looked like a sale of their life-story rights. Five plaintiffs say they signed in December 2019, and Frank followed in January 2020.

According to the complaint, the agreement called for five annual payments of $690,000 per plaintiff, minus a 6% commission.

It also required private arbitration and released claims against the estate, the plaintiffs say. They allege that if one family member disclosed the alleged abuse, the agreement could force the whole family to return the money.

The plaintiffs say they hired another lawyer after Freedman returned in 2024 and suggested the estate should pay them more.

“Had Freedman explained to Plaintiffs the implications of any of these provisions, they never would have signed the Agreement,” their lawyers wrote.

Four siblings, Edward, Dominic, Marie-Nicole and Aldo, separately sued in February over alleged childhood sexual abuse.

Estate lawyer Martin Singer previously rejected their allegations, calling them “a desperate money grab” in Rolling Stone.

The magazine said it couldn’t immediately reach Freedman about the new suit.

A federal judge sent the separate case to arbitration in August, and a joint November 10 filing confirms it is still proceeding there. The siblings spoke about the underlying allegations in an interview with 60 Minutes Australia.

The plaintiffs are seeking damages to be determined at trial, punitive damages and legal fees in the new suit against Freedman.

item.title: Company Defends “George Floyd The Musical” Ad Seeking Rappers & Comedic Singers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Playbill pulls a casting notice seeking comedic singers for a George Floyd album and apologizes for approving the listing.
item.content:encoded:
George Floyd‘s name appeared in a call for comedic singers on Playbill’s jobs board this week.

The theater publication took the ad down and apologized Thursday after readers objected to a cast recording being pitched as dark comedy.

Playbill said in its Instagram statement that its jobs team approved the listing Wednesday afternoon. The company said leadership ordered its removal after learning about it and started reviewing how job ads get approved.

“We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward,” Playbill said.

The ad came from Busted Broadway, an independent label founded by composer Kevin Lynch.

A separate casting notice on DirectSubmit describes a paid studio recording in northern New Jersey. A notice on Backstage also sought a lead rapper.

The label’s project page still lists the title after the Playbill notice came down.

Busted Broadway makes concept albums that it markets as dark comedy.

The casting notice asked performers whether they were comfortable with provocative material, and the label defended the project in its own Instagram statement.

“Our George Floyd the Musical is not making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd,” Busted Broadway said.

Floyd was killed in Minneapolis on May 25, 2020, when police officer Derek Chauvin pressed his knee against Floyd’s neck while he was handcuffed.

His murder set off protests across the United States and abroad. A Minnesota jury convicted Chauvin of murder, and he later pleaded guilty in federal court to violating Floyd’s civil rights.

Before his name became a rallying cry, Floyd was known in Houston as Big Floyd. He rapped on DJ Screw’s mixtapes, and rapper Trae Tha Truth took ABC News back to the Third Ward where Floyd was raised.

Trae and Bun B also organized a Houston march with Floyd’s family days after his death.

Hip-Hop’s response stretched from the street to the studio. Lil Baby released “The Bigger Picture” during the protests in 2020, opening the record with news audio about Floyd’s murder before rapping about police violence.

The DirectSubmit notice offers performers $150 for a session and says the company plans to record through the end of 2026.

item.title: Mad Skillz Puts Richmond Teens First With Holiday Gift Drive
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mad Skillz joins Richmond's Art Bus gift drive, where books, headphones and sports gear can help make a teen's holiday.
item.content:encoded:
Mad Skillz is teaming up with Richmond’s transit agency to collect holiday gifts for local kids, with a special push to reach teenagers.

The rapper will help kick off “Santa’s Got Skillz” at the Richmond Christmas Parade on December 5, where he’ll ride with Greater Richmond Transit Company employees as the agency’s Art Bus follows.

The plan is to fill the bus with new, unwrapped gifts and get them to families through four local nonprofits, GRTC announced.

Those partners are ASK Childhood Cancer Foundation, Peter Paul Development Center, Ronald McDonald House Charities of Richmond and Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Richmond.

The drive especially wants gifts for ages 13 to 17, including headphones, art supplies, sports gear or games. The Art Bus will start taking donations after the parade and make more stops December 9 through 12.

“Thank you to Mad Skillz for inspiring us to do big things right here in our community, where it matters most,” Richmond Mayor Danny Avula said.

The agency said the Boys & Girls Club was among the groups that helped inspire him.

In August, Skillz offered to buy school shoes for kids he met shopping with their families at Richmond-area malls. He told parents he tries to do it every year before classes start, and said he helped 13 families on the first day.

Richmond has been part of his work for decades.

He started rapping on the University of Richmond’s radio station and returned as an artist-in-residence to help teach a course on Hip-Hop.

He told AllHipHop about fighting for a place for Virginia in rap before his spoken-word records earned him Grammys.

“From the time I started rapping and taking music seriously all I knew was that I was proud of where I was from,” Skillz said.

His first Grammy came this year for Words For Days Vol. 1, which featured 14 Richmond-area collaborators.

The Recording Academy has since nominated him in the same spoken-word poetry album category for A Hero And A Villain, his third straight nomination.

After the parade, the first collection stop is the Willow Lawn Target at 5401 West Broad Street from 1 to 3 P.M.

item.title: Nelly Moves Black And White Ball To Bigger Venue For Its 15th Edition
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nelly's Black and White Ball moves to St. Charles for its 15th edition, supporting Make-A-Wish Missouri and college scholarships.
item.content:encoded:
Nelly is moving his Black and White Ball out of downtown St. Louis for its 15th edition. Organizers announced that the December 13 fundraiser will take place at Ameristar Casino Resort Spa in St. Charles, Missouri, instead of the Four Seasons, FOX 2 St. Louis reported.

Nelly said the extra room came from a bigger commitment from sponsors this year.

“The Black and White Ball has always been about giving back to our city’s youth and celebrating our love for St. Louis,” he said in the announcement.

The money raised at the gala will help Make-A-Wish Missouri grant wishes to children with critical illnesses.

The event will also fund college scholarships for St. Louis students attending Harris-Stowe State University, the city’s historically Black university.

The scholarship tie goes back years. Nelly hosted the first ball in 2006 and kept it going annually through 2016.

When he brought the fundraiser back in 2023, scholarships for local students and support for Make-A-Wish remained part of the program.

Students received scholarships at the Four Seasons last December, when Olympic gold medalist Jackie Joyner-Kersee received the ball’s Legend Award.

Nelly also used the night to grant a child’s wish for a family trip to Disney World.

Past editions have drawn artists including Ashanti, Janet Jackson, Busta Rhymes, Monica and Boyz II Men, alongside St. Louis sports figures. Cardinals Hall of Famer Ozzie Smith received the first Legend Award after the gala returned in 2023.

Nelly spoke about giving computers, bicycles and scholarships to kids in an earlier interview with AllHipHop.

The St. Louis rapper tied that work to a belief that his hometown should see some of the benefits of his career, alongside his plans for business in the city.

Derrty Entertainment and Synergy Productions are producing the event, with the Daugherty Foundation as title sponsor. The foundation is among the groups helping put the gala in a larger room. The new venue still puts the event in the St. Louis region, across the Missouri River from St. Louis County.

The organizers’ announcement named past guests but did not name this year’s performers or list ticket prices.

item.title: Mannie Fresh, Juvenile & T.I. Bring Their Southern Rap History To Jazz Fest
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Mannie Fresh, Juvenile and T.I. share a 2027 Jazz Fest billing, with LL Cool J, Wyclef Jean and Big Freedia on weekend two.
item.content:encoded:
Mannie Fresh is bringing Juvenile and T.I. to New Orleans Jazz Fest under one billing.

The festival announced its 2027 lineup Thursday (November 19), placing the trio on the second weekend alongside LL Cool J, Wyclef Jean and Big Freedia.

Mannie and Juvenile have spent much of this fall on the same bill. Both were part of the Cash Money & No Limit Tour, the arena run led by Birdman and Master P that included a September stop at New Orleans’ Smoothie King Center.

The new festival date pairs them with an Atlanta rapper whose own work with Mannie stretches back two decades.

Mannie produced T.I.’s “Top Back” for his 2006 album King.

In an interview with Splice, he recalled trying to get T.I. signed to Cash Money years earlier and said the record started with Juvenile: “And the crazy thing is, ‘Top Back’ was actually Juvie’s song.”

Fresh added, “And I had Tip do the hook before Juvie walked into the studio.”

All three revisited how the beat changed hands on Mannie and Juvenile’s Still 400 podcast.

Before that, Mannie had helped turn Juvenile’s New Orleans club records into national hits.

He produced “Back That Azz Up” and changed the drums on “Ha,” a song Juvenile was already taking to local crowds before recording 400 Degreez.

The two have kept finding new ways to play those records. For Juvenile’s Tiny Desk concert, Mannie worked alongside the 400 Degreez Band, with New Orleans musicians Trombone Shorty and Jon Batiste joining the set.

The second weekend runs April 29 through May 2 at the Fair Grounds Race Course.

LL Cool J is billed with DJ Z-Trip and Technician The DJ, while Chaka Khan is booked for the opening weekend, April 22 through 25. New Orleans acts on the second weekend also include Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue, the Soul Rebels and Rebirth Brass Band.

item.title: Jazzy Jay’s NYC Birthday Brings Out DJ Premier, Red Alert & Hip-Hop Pioneers
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: DJ Premier, Kool DJ Red Alert, Crazy Legs and Melle Mel celebrated Jazzy Jay, whose records helped get Def Jam started.
item.content:encoded:
Jazzy Jay marked his birthday with a Hip-Hop History Month gathering in New York. DJ Premier, Kool DJ Red Alert, Crazy Legs and Melle Mel gathered Wednesday (November 18) at Hidden Tiger at Fat Social Club in the East Village.

The lineup brought together DJs, breakers and MCs.

Crazy Legs came out of the Rock Steady Crew’s breaking scene, Melle Mel was an MC in Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five, and Premier took his production from Gang Starr to records with artists such as Nas.

For Red Alert and Jazzy Jay, the connection goes back to family and two turntables.

Red Alert recalled teaching his cousin the basics before Jay started getting work in the Bronx.

Jay played on Disco King Mario’s sound system and later helped bring Red Alert into the Zulu Nation’s circle.

“Jazzy kept talking to him about me, ‘Put my cousin down,'” Red Alert recalled of Afrika Bambaataa.

Jazzy Jay used another sound system, the one he’d built into his Chevy Caprice, when he and Rick Rubin were working on “It’s Yours” with T La Rock.

He told AllHipHop they’d test mixes in the car and go back upstairs if the bass wasn’t right.

“We’d park, pump the sounds, and sell twelve-inches. That was the beginning days of Def Jam.”

Cornell University Library’s original 12-inch shows both the Partytime and Def Jam catalog numbers.

The archive makes a distinction: “It’s Yours” carried the Def Jam name before Rubin and Russell Simmons put out their first record as a team, LL Cool J’s “I Need a Beat.”

Jazzy Jay also recorded “Def Jam,” backed with “Cold Chillin’ in the Spot,” with Simmons on the flip side. The 1985 release put Jay’s scratching and electronically altered voice on the title track.

item.title: FullyGangJit Dies At 25, A Day Before New Single Arrives
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: FullyGangJit, a 25-year-old Baton Rouge rapper, dies in a shooting one day before his collaboration with Bty Beedo arrives.
item.content:encoded:
FullyGangJit, an independent Baton Rouge rapper who put out a series of projects through 25/7 Records, was shot and killed in his home city on November 17.

He was 25. A collaboration with Bty Beedo arrived on streaming services a day after his death.

Baton Rouge police identified the rapper as Micah Farlough and said the shooting happened around 12:47 A.M. at a market at 3916 Plank Road, WBRZ reported.

Farlough was taken to a hospital, where he died. The East Baton Rouge Parish Coroner’s Office said it received a call from the hospital around 2:50 a.m.

Detectives had not named a suspect or identified a motive when they released Farlough’s name.

FullyGangJit had spent the past few years building a catalog with collaborators from the local scene.

In an interview with SquadTV, he discussed his move from athletics to music, how he picked his stage name and what it took to keep putting out records on his own. The conversation also covered how he developed his sound in Baton Rouge.

Among his earlier recordings was a 2023 appearance on BWay Never Broke Again’s “Me vs Me, Pt. 2,” a group track that also features Mg Woodie, Monewaypeso and Stacks Osama.

By 2025, he was releasing projects under his own name, including FullyVille, FullyVille2 and Still Bleeding. Monewaypeso returned for “DSG Shit” on FullyVille and “Confirm The Kill” on the sequel.

The artist’s streaming catalog shows his releases continued this year with Product Of The Trenches.

He released a deluxe edition on August 7, bringing the album to 19 songs. Longtime collaborator Tmh Joker appeared on the album cut “Pick Em Up” and had already worked with him on “Triple Threat.”

The record released after his death was “Buss It Baby,” the November 18 single credited to FullyGangJit and Bty Beedo on the same label.

Baton Rouge police asked anyone with information about the shooting to call the Capital Region Crime Stoppers tip line at (225) 344-7867.
